import ctypes
import sys
import os

def gsl_fcmp_py(x1, x2, epsilon=1e-10):
    # Load libraries with correct order and global resolution
    cblas = ctypes.CDLL('/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so', mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
    gsl = ctypes.CDLL('/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so')
    
    # Configure function prototype
    gsl.gsl_fcmp.argtypes = [ctypes.c_double, ctypes.c_double, ctypes.c_double]
    gsl.gsl_fcmp.restype = ctypes.c_int
    
    # Call the C function
    return gsl.gsl_fcmp(ctypes.c_double(x1), ctypes.c_double(x2), ctypes.c_double(epsilon))

def assert_test():
    # Test approximate equality
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1.0, 1.0 + 1e-12) == 0  # Essentially equal
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1.0, 1.0 + 1e-11) == 0   # Equal within default epsilon
    
    # Test greater than
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1.1, 1.0) == 1          # Clearly greater
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1.0000001, 1.0, 1e-8) == 1  # Slightly greater with appropriate epsilon
    
    # Test less than
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(0.9, 1.0) == -1         # Clearly less
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(0.9999999, 1.0, 1e-8) == -1  # Slightly less with appropriate epsilon
    
    # Test with custom epsilon
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1.0, 1.01, 0.1) == 0    # Equal with large epsilon
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1.0, 1.01, 0.001) == -1 # Different with small epsilon
    
    # Test edge cases
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(0.0, 0.0) == 0          # Zero equality
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(-1.0, -1.0) == 0        # Negative equality
    assert gsl_fcmp_py(1e10, 1e10 + 100.0, 1e-4) == 0  # Large numbers with appropriate relative tolerance
    
    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
